q2.answer: The resume position is download_last_saved_id in the single-row sync_state table in SQLite. The same transaction that saves a page's rows into the download generation also advances that cursor, so the cursor always matches the saved products. A crash before the commit loses the page, and it is fetched again on resume.

q3.answer: Before the first page, the client calls POST /sync/begin and stores the watermark, which is the highest committed change_seq. After all pages are saved, it replays every change after the watermark from the changes feed into the downloaded copy (the drain). Because rows become visible in change_seq order, anything edited after its page was read appears in the feed. Anything edited before is already in the page, and replaying it is harmless. Deletes arrive as tombstones.

q5.answer: The new catalogue is built in the inactive generation table (product_g0 or product_g1), which is emptied at the start. Pages and then the drain go into it while reps keep reading the active generation. It becomes the one the app reads in a single swap transaction after the drain finishes. That transaction sets active_gen to the download generation, sets live_cursor_seq to the drain position and sets download_status to none.

q9.answer: It applies the incoming row only if its change_seq is greater than or equal to the stored row's, or if no row is stored. An incoming delete removes the row if it is present and does nothing if it is absent. The same rule covers page rows, feed changes and pages fetched again after a crash. Equal change_seq means the same version, so writing it again is harmless.

q10.answer: The incremental pull starts at live_cursor_seq, which is null until the first swap. The swap sets it to the drain's final position. After that, each changes response is applied to the active generation in one transaction that also sets live_cursor_seq to next_seq. The position moves forward only when that response's changes are committed. A failure leaves it at the last committed response.

q11.answer: The feed is a read of products with change_seq greater than after_seq, in change_seq order, 1,000 per response, supported by an index on change_seq. Each response carries next_seq and has_more. Deletes are soft-delete tombstone rows in the same feed, sent as {id, deleted:true, change_seq}. They are kept for 7 days. The purge job records purged_through_seq beforehand, and a request from before it gets a 410 resync_required response.
